title: Phnom Penh and Angkor Wat Luxury Family Guide: Siem Reap Temples, Raffles Grand Hotel & Private Tours
excerpt: Cambodia offers one of Asia's most rewarding luxury family adventures — from the temples of Angkor at dawn to the riverside elegance of Phnom Penh. The definitive guide to experiencing Cambodia in five-star comfort with children, including Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor, Shinta Mani, and private temple tours.
author: Luxury Family Travel Asia Team
content:
Why Cambodia Belongs on Every Luxury Family Itinerary

Cambodia is often overlooked by luxury families in favour of Thailand, Vietnam, or Indonesia. This is a mistake. Cambodia offers a depth of historical wonder and cultural authenticity that no other Southeast Asian destination can match, delivered through a surprisingly sophisticated luxury infrastructure. The temples of Angkor are the largest religious monument in the world — a scale that captures children's imaginations in a way few man-made structures can. The service culture in Cambodia's finest hotels is warm, intuitive, and genuinely welcoming to children. And the cost advantage over Thailand or Singapore means families can afford experiences — private guides, helicopter tours, exclusive dining — that would cost double elsewhere.

This guide covers the two essential destinations for a luxury family trip to Cambodia: Siem Reap for the Angkor temples, and Phnom Penh for the capital's riverside elegance and tragic-but-important history. It focuses on the hotels, guides, and experiences that make Cambodia accessible and enriching for children of all ages, from temple-toddlers to curious teenagers.

Siem Reap: The Gateway to Angkor

Where to Stay

1. Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor — Colonial Elegance, 100 Years of Service

The Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor has welcomed travellers to Siem Reap since 1932. After a comprehensive renovation in 2021, the hotel balances its colonial-era grandeur with modern family comfort. The property occupies 15 acres of lush gardens in the heart of Siem Reap, a 10-minute walk from the Old Market and Pub Street, and a 20-minute drive from the Angkor temple complex.

For families, the Landmark Suite (100 sqm) or the two-bedroom Residence Suite (200 sqm) are the best choices. The Landmark Suite features a separate living room with a dining table for six, a master bedroom with a marble bathroom and deep soaking tub, and a private balcony overlooking the gardens. The Residence Suite adds a second bedroom with twin beds and en-suite bathroom, a study, and a private garden with plunge pool — ideal for multi-generational families. The suites are located in the hotel's original 1932 wing, with high ceilings, ceiling fans, and plantation shutters that evoke a bygone era of travel while providing modern amenities — Dyson hair dryers, Nespresso machines, and high-speed Wi-Fi.

Family facilities and services: The hotel's charming children's programme includes Cambodian cooking classes where children learn to make fresh spring rolls and amok (the national curry), traditional dance lessons where a local instructor teaches children Apsara dance moves, and a 'Little Treasures' treasure hunt through the hotel's gardens. The large free-form pool is a family favourite — children are welcome with flotation devices provided by the pool team, and the poolside service includes fresh fruit skewers and mocktails. The hotel offers a dedicated nanny service (US$15-20 per hour, pre-arranged) through a partnered agency of experienced, English-speaking carers.

What the Raffles butler does for families: The same legendary butler service that defines Raffles Singapore applies here — butlers unpack for families, coordinate temple tour itineraries, pre-arrange breakfast picnic packs for pre-dawn Angkor Wat visits, and provide a dedicated WhatsApp number for requests during your stay. The concierge team specialises in family temple tours (see below). Rates: From US$350/night for a State Room; US$600-1,200/night for suites. Book Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor on Booking.com — their 'Colonial Family Escape' package includes breakfast, one children's cooking class, and a sunset cocktail at the Elephant Bar (alcoholic for parents, virgin mocktails for children).

2. Shinta Mani Angkor — Bill Bensley's Playful Masterpiece

Shinta Mani Angkor — The Bensley Collection is a 10-suite boutique hotel that is anything but traditional. Designed by the legendary Bill Bensley, the hotel is a riot of colour and whimsy — think hand-painted Khmer murals, jewel-toned silks, and playful design touches that delight children as much as adults. Each suite is themed after a different aspect of Cambodian culture, from the sugar palm tree to the Mekong River.

The one-bedroom Bensley Suite (80 sqm) accommodates families of up to four with a king bed and a sofa bed. The suite features an outdoor shower (enclosed for privacy), a private plunge pool, and a terrace overlooking the hotel's tropical gardens. The interior design makes every surface an experience — children will discover hidden animals in the murals, try on the traditional Cambodian hats provided as decoration, and ask endless questions about the colours and patterns. The hotel's pool bar serves the best passionfruit mojito (non-alcoholic for children) in Siem Reap.

Family facilities: The hotel's pool is small but perfectly maintained. The complimentary tuk-tuk service takes families to Pub Street and the Night Market (5 minutes) or to the Angkor Ticket Office (15 minutes). The concierge team excels at arranging private tuk-tuk tours of the temples — the open-air tuk-tuk is a highlight for children who find enclosed vehicles claustrophobic in the heat. Rates: From US$400/night. Best for: Design-loving families, couples with younger children (the boutique scale means fewer facilities but more personalised service), and families who want a uniquely Cambodian aesthetic experience.

3. Park Hyatt Siem Reap — Ultra-Modern Comfort

The Park Hyatt Siem Reap offers a modern, minimalist alternative to the colonial grandeur of Raffles. The hotel's 104 rooms and 24 suites are arranged around a central courtyard with a reflecting pool and frangipani trees. The design is contemporary Khmer — clean lines, warm timbers, and local art.

For families, the two-bedroom Park Suite (150 sqm) offers a master bedroom, a children's bedroom with twin beds and bright decor, a living room with dining table, and a private terrace. The suite connects directly to the lap pool (25-metre) — children can swim from their room. The hotel's Kids' Club (ages 4-12) offers supervised craft activities, Khmer storybook reading, and pool games. The concierge team specialises in family-friendly temple tours and can arrange the 'Khmer Family Experience' — a full-day itinerary that includes temple visits, a cooking class, and a sunset at Pre Rup temple. Rates: From US$250/night for a standard room; US$500-900/night for suites. Best for: Families who prefer modern design, want reliable Hyatt service standards, and value the location near the Old Market and nightlife.

Experiencing Angkor Wat with Children: The Art of the Private Tour

Visiting the Angkor temple complex with children requires strategy. The complex covers 400 square kilometres and contains over 1,000 temples — a standard group tour tries to cover too much, too fast, at the wrong time of day. The luxury family approach is to see less, but better — three or four temples over two days, visited at optimal times with a private guide who specialises in children.

The private guide is the single most important investment in your Siem Reap itinerary. A great guide translates the history of Angkor into stories that children can grasp — the battle between gods and demons churning the ocean of milk, the monkey king Hanuman's adventures, the daily life of 12th-century Khmer people visible in the temple carvings. Contact the Raffles or Shinta Mani concierge before arrival and request a guide who works regularly with children. The best guides (those licensed by the Ministry of Tourism with demonstrated family experience) cost approximately US$60-80 per day — worth every dollar.

The family-friendly Angkor itinerary:

  • Day 1, 5:00 AM — Angkor Wat at Sunrise: This is non-negotiable. Wake the children early (the hotel provides a pre-dawn breakfast pack), arrive at Angkor Wat before the gates open, and watch the sun rise behind the five iconic towers reflected in the lotus pond. The experience is magical, the crowds are manageable at dawn, and children remember the silhouettes against the pink sky for years. Your private guide leads a 90-minute tour of the main temple before the heat and crowds build. Return to the hotel for breakfast and pool time by 8:30 AM.
  • Day 1, 3:00 PM — Bayon Temple and the Smiling Faces: The Bayon's 216 massive stone faces — each with a peaceful, enigmatic smile — are the most child-friendly attraction in Angkor. Children love counting the faces, finding the one that looks like a family member, and learning that each face represents a different aspect of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara. The temple's relatively compact size (90 minutes is sufficient) and the open-air galleries make it ideal for an afternoon visit when the light is golden.
  • Day 2, 7:00 AM — Ta Prohm (the Tomb Raider Temple): Ta Prohm is every child's favourite temple. Giant silk-cotton and strangler fig trees have grown through the ruins, their roots wrapping around the stone walls and ceilings. Children can play 'jungle explorer' while learning how nature reclaims human creations. The temple takes approximately 60-90 minutes to explore and is best visited early — by 9:30 AM the tour groups arrive in force.
  • Day 2, Late Afternoon — Pre Rup Temple Sunset: Pre Rup is a temple-mountain with wide, shallow steps that children can climb safely. The sunset views over the surrounding forest, with distant temple towers poking through the trees, are spectacular. Your guide brings a blanket and snacks — settle at the top platform and watch the sky change colour while the children spot bats emerging from the forest below.

Logistical tips for temple days: Hire a private air-conditioned vehicle with cool-box rather than an open tuk-tuk for the main temple visits — the 3-minute walk from car to temple entrance is fine, but the 20-minute drive between temples in midday heat is brutal without AC. Pack a small bag with water (the guide carries a cooler), snacks (granola bars, dried mango), sunscreen, hats, and a change of t-shirts for children who sweat through their clothes (this will happen by 10 AM). Most temples have shade and rest areas — plan breaks every 45 minutes.

Private helicopter tour: For families with older children (8+), a 30-minute helicopter tour over Angkor Wat offers perspectives impossible from the ground. The tour departs from Siem Reap International Airport and flies over Angkor Wat, Angkor Thom, and the surrounding jungle. The cost is approximately US$800-1,200 for a family of four — book through the Raffles or Shinta Mani concierge. This is the single most impressive family experience in Cambodia.

Family Dining in Siem Reap

  • Raffles Grand Hotel's Dining Room: French-Khmer cuisine in a columned colonial dining room. The children's menu features familiar classics alongside gentle Khmer introductions — chicken amok, fish with rice. The Sunday brunch is exceptional. From US$30-50 per adult, children under 12 half-price.
  • Malis Restaurant: Siem Reap's finest Khmer restaurant, with a garden setting and a children's menu. The prahok ktis (pork dip with coconut, served with fresh vegetables) is a national dish that most children enjoy. From US$15-25 per person.
  • Chanrey Tree: Riverside Khmer restaurant with a private garden area perfect for families. The beef lok lak is a safe entry point for cautious young eaters. Cooking classes also offered — a 2-hour family class costs US$35 per person.

Phnom Penh: Capital Elegance and Important History

Where to Stay

Raffles Hotel Le Royal — Phnom Penh's Colonial Treasure

Raffles Hotel Le Royal, opened in 1929 and meticulously restored, is the finest address in Phnom Penh. The hotel occupies 2.5 hectares in the city centre, with mature gardens, two swimming pools (including a 50-metre lap pool), and 175 rooms and suites. The design is French colonial with Khmer touches — think terrazzo floors, ceiling fans, and verandahs overlooking the pool.

For families, the Landmark Suite (75 sqm) or the two-bedroom Residence Suite (175 sqm) are the best choices. The Landmark Suite features a separate living room, a master bedroom with a walk-in wardrobe, and a balcony overlooking the main pool. The Residence Suite adds a second bedroom, a dining room, and a private plunge pool. The hotel's location near the Royal Palace, the National Museum, and the riverside promenade makes sightseeing effortless on foot.

Family highlights at Raffles Hotel Le Royal: The hotel's pool is the largest hotel pool in Phnom Penh — children splash for hours while parents lounge on the surrounding sunbeds. The hotel's Living Room serves afternoon tea (a favourite with children — the scones and pastries are excellent) and the Elephant Bar serves evening cocktails. The concierge team arranges private tours of the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda (children love the diamond-studded Buddha and the floor made of 5,000 silver tiles), a private boat cruise on the Mekong River at sunset, and a guided tour of the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Killing Fields — the latter is suitable for children aged 10+ but parents should preview the content and decide based on their child's maturity. Rates: From US$300/night for a State Room; US$500-1,000/night for suites. Book Raffles Hotel Le Royal on Booking.com — their 'Phnom Penh Family Escape' package includes breakfast, airport transfers, and a private sunset river cruise.

Alternatives: The Rosewood Phnom Penh and Sofitel Phnom Penh Phokeethra

The Rosewood Phnom Penh (floors 29-45 of the Vattanac Capital Tower) offers the best city views in Phnom Penh. The 37th-floor pool is spectacular. The two-bedroom Residence (170 sqm) on the 43rd floor offers panoramic views of the Mekong River and the city — children will spend hours at the floor-to-ceiling windows spotting boats on the river. Rates from US$350/night. The Sofitel Phnom Penh Phokeethra offers excellent value with a large pool, a children's club, and spacious connecting rooms starting from US$150/night — the best mid-range luxury option in the capital.

Family Experiences in Phnom Penh

  • Private sunset cruise on the Mekong River: A 2-hour cruise with drinks and canapés as the sun sets over the Mekong. Children spot fishing boats, river dolphins (rare but present), and the illuminated Royal Palace as darkness falls. Arrange through Raffles concierge. From US$150 for a private boat for a family of six.
  • Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda: The Royal Palace's throne hall, the Napoleon III Pavilion, and the Silver Pagoda's 5,000 silver floor tiles and emerald Buddha statue. Children aged 6+ appreciate the history; younger children enjoy running in the palace gardens. Allow 90 minutes. Entry: US$10 per adult, children under 12 free.
  • Phnom Penh Food Tour by cyclo: A private cyclo (Cambodian bicycle rickshaw) tour through the city's market and street food scene. The guide selects safe, mild dishes suitable for children — fresh spring rolls, grilled corn, fried bananas, and sugar cane juice. The cyclo ride itself is the highlight — children love the open-air journey through the city's bustling streets. From US$40 per person, including food.
  • Koh Dach (Silk Island) day trip: A 30-minute ferry from Phnom Penh to a Mekong island where families visit silk-weaving villages, see traditional Khmer houses on stilts, and ride bicycles through rural countryside. The round trip takes half a day and is suitable for all ages. The Raffles concierge can arrange a private guide and picnic lunch. From US$100 for a family of four.

Getting to Cambodia and Getting Around

Siem Reap International Airport receives direct flights from Singapore (2 hours), Bangkok (1 hour), Kuala Lumpur (2 hours), Hanoi (2 hours), and Hong Kong (2.5 hours). Vietnam Airlines and Singapore Airlines offer the best business-class products. Phnom Penh International Airport connects to the same hubs plus direct flights from Seoul, Tokyo, and Dubai. A domestic flight between Phnom Penh and Siem Reap takes 45 minutes — Cambodia Angkor Air operates the route with reasonable business-class seats at approximately US$120 per person.

Private drivers are the safest option for families. The road between Phnom Penh and Siem Reap (6 hours) is now sealed and well-maintained but not recommended for families — fly instead. Within each city, a private car with driver costs approximately US$30-50 per day through any hotel concierge — the best investment for families, as tuk-tuks are charming but hot and bumpy for young children.

Best Time to Visit Cambodia

November to February is the ideal period for family travel. Temperatures are 22-30°C, humidity is low, and rainfall is minimal. This is also peak season — book hotels 3-4 months in advance. March to May is hot (30-38°C) with low rainfall. Temple visits should start at 5 AM and finish by 10 AM. June to October is the rainy season — afternoon downpours are intense but brief (30-60 minutes) and the countryside is at its greenest. Hotel rates drop 30-50% but temple experiences are compromised by the heat and occasional flooding.

Health and Safety Considerations

Phnom Penh and Siem Reap have excellent private medical facilities. Royal Phnom Penh Hospital and Apex Cambodia Clinic in Siem Reap have English-speaking doctors and can handle most medical issues. For serious cases, medical evacuation to Bangkok (1 hour flight) is covered by most travel insurance policies — ensure your policy covers helicopter evacuation from temple sites. Recommended vaccinations: Hepatitis A, Typhoid, and Tetanus. Japanese Encephalitis is recommended for families spending time in rural areas near Siem Reap's outer temple circuit. Malaria risk is low in Siem Reap and Phnom Penh — most luxury hotel rooms are sealed and air-conditioned, making mosquito exposure minimal. Dengue fever is present year-round — use DEET-based repellent consistently, particularly at dawn and dusk.

Food safety note: Do not drink tap water anywhere in Cambodia — even luxury hotels advise against it. Bottled water is provided in hotel rooms and available at every shop (US$0.50 per litre). Street food is generally safe when prepared fresh and hot — stick to stalls with high turnover. Meals at luxury hotels and fine-dining restaurants are safe. Carry electrolyte sachets for hot days — children dehydrate quickly in the Cambodian heat.

Sample Itinerary: 7 Days in Cambodia

Days 1-3: Siem Reap — Stay at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or Shinta Mani Angkor. Day 1: Arrival, pool afternoon, evening at Raffles' Elephant Bar. Day 2: 5 AM Angkor Wat sunrise, Bayon morning, pool afternoon, dinner at Malis. Day 3: 7 AM Ta Prohm, 2 PM Pre Rup sunset, Cambodian cooking class for children at Raffles.

Day 4: Transfer — Morning pool, 1 PM flight to Phnom Penh (45 minutes). Check into Raffles Hotel Le Royal. Evening sunset cruise on the Mekong River.

Days 5-7: Phnom Penh — Day 5: Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda morning, afternoon pool, evening food tour by cyclo. Day 6: Optional Silk Island day trip or Tuol Sleng / Killing Fields for older children. Day 7: Final morning at the pool, depart from Phnom Penh International Airport.

Estimated budget for a family of four: US$5,000-8,000 for a 7-day trip including luxury accommodation at Raffles, private guides, domestic flights, and all meals and experiences. This is exceptional value — a comparable itinerary in Thailand would cost 40-60% more.

The Luxury Family Verdict: Cambodia offers Asia's most culturally enriching luxury family experience at prices that are almost unreasonable. The temples of Angkor are genuinely awe-inspiring for children — the scale, the carvings, the jungle setting make everything else feel small. The Raffles properties in Siem Reap and Phnom Penh provide the colonial-era service that families with young children genuinely benefit from — butlers who anticipate needs, concierges who arrange everything, and a warmth of service that comes naturally in Khmer culture. The investment in a private guide — the single best money you will spend in Cambodia — transforms temple visits from hot marches to living history lessons. If your family values cultural depth over beach time, Cambodia will be your favourite destination in Southeast Asia. Book hotels on Booking.com for the best cancellation terms.
